title: Claudinite pack manifest
description: THE PACK MANIFEST SPEC — the single declarative statement of what a pack.json may and must carry. A pack declares DATA here and names its code by filename: sibling .mjs modules the loader imports (rules, an env block, a detect predicate that needs real logic). Editors validate and complete a pack.json against this file via its $schema pointer; the loader validates against it too, so a malformed manifest surfaces as a blocking config error at load — canon packs and a consumer's own local packs alike. An undeclared field is an error: this is the closed vocabulary of a pack, so a typo (rule:, skill:) fails loudly instead of being silently ignored forever.

$schema.description: the relative path to this schema, so an editor validates and completes the file

id.description: the pack id, matching its directory name

ruleRoutingGuidance.description: what belongs in this pack and what does not, each at most 20 words — both sides are emitted as one row of a table every session loads

belongs.description: the kind of content this pack owns, in at most 20 words

excludes.description: what belongs elsewhere and which pack owns it, in at most 20 words

badge.description: the pack badge filename, resolved off the pack directory

marker.description: a human-readable glob naming what detect looks for, or null

detect.description: the repo fingerprint — null when the declaration alone is authoritative, a tracked-path predicate as data, or a detect.mjs filename when recognizing the technology needs real logic (reading file CONTENT, parsing a manifest)

prose.description: the RULES.md filename injected at session start, or null

seededByDefault.description: whether bootstrap --init seeds this pack everywhere

requires.description: pack ids this pack depends on, resolved when the declaration is written

contributes.description: rules addressed to another pack, keyed by that pack id — each value the filenames of the modules whose default export is the contributed DATA (a contribution is never a cross-pack code import)

contributedRules.description: the module whose default export is the seam interpreting other packs' contributions to this one

env.description: an environment requirement the base image does not ship — inline when setup and probe are fixed shell, or an env.mjs filename when they are functions of the project's per-pack config

skills.description: the skill directory names bundled under this pack's skills/

worldRules.description: the rule modules auditing repo state (check_the_world), by filename

workRules.description: the rule modules judging the current change and session (check_the_work), by filename

helpers.description: the pack-root .mjs modules that are NOT rules — shared libraries, hook entry points — named so every module in the pack directory is accounted for and an undeclared rule cannot hide

moduleFile.description: a sibling module filename in the pack directory — a bare name, never a path

detectSpec.description: a fingerprint as data: true when ANY tracked path satisfies every matcher declared under trackedPath

trackedPath.description: the matchers one tracked path must ALL satisfy; where a matcher takes a list, any entry satisfies it

endsWith.description: a suffix of the repo-relative path

matches.description: a regular expression the whole path must match

maxDepth.description: the most path segments allowed — 1 is the repo root, 2 one directory down

envSpec.description: an inline environment requirement — fixed shell, no dependence on the project's config

label.description: what is being installed, named in the setup log and in the missing-requirement alert

setup.description: the shell that installs the requirement, run in the checkout at environment-image build

probe.description: the shell that exits 0 when the requirement is actually present

id.description: the question id, unique within the pack — the key the answer is recorded under

prompt.description: the question as it is put to the adopter

distill.description: what the interviewer does with the answer — which config the answer sets, or that it records as intent

shell.description: a shell fragment — one string, or the lines of a script, which the loader joins with newlines so a multi-line install reads as lines instead of one escaped blob

stringOrList.description: one string, or a non-empty list of them
